turns.response_markdown: Tides are the regular rises and falls of ocean water caused mainly by the Moon’s gravity pulling on Earth’s oceans, with the Sun also contributing. As Earth rotates, coastlines move through areas of higher and lower water levels. Most places experience two high tides and two low tides each day, though patterns vary. The alignment of the Sun, Moon, and Earth creates stronger “spring tides,” while right-angle positions create weaker “neap tides.” Tides influence coastal ecosystems, navigation, fishing, and shoreline processes. They are a powerful example of natural oceanic rhythms.
